thought.text: Asset serving and syntax are good. Let me attempt to actually execute the app. First let me try the Vite dev server (documented dev path) and also inspect whether the bundle contains app bootstrap logic.

reasoning_content:
The bundle passes syntax check. Now let me try to actually load the portal in a DOM environment. jsdom is available. But executing masterportal.js in jsdom may be heavy and involve WebGL which jsdom doesn't support. Let me try a lightweight approach — actually, best evidence is to run the masterportal bundle in jsdom and see if it initializes. But it's an ES module. jsdom can't easily execute ES modules.

Alternative: Use the dev server (vite) to confirm the app builds/serves. Actually the build already succeeded and artifacts serve. Let me try to execute the bundle with jsdom + a minimal setup. That's likely to fail due to missing browser APIs (WebGL, canvas), which wouldn't necessarily indicate installation failure.

Let me think about what constitutes "operational". The guide describes hosting a prebuilt portal on a web server. The installation used source build. The portal index.html loads masterportal.js which mounts to #masterportal-root. Let me try to verify the bundle executes to the point of rendering using jsdom, tolerating expected browser API gaps.

Actually, a cleaner check: the bundle's structure and the fact it references config. Let me try running it in jsdom.

Let me at least attempt to load it and capture whether it starts executing (e.g., defines Vue app). Let me write a jsdom harness.

Actually masterportal.js is a huge ES module importing relative files. Serving via HTTP with type=module in jsdom - jsdom doesn't support ES modules script execution. So that won't work.

Better: use vite dev server to serve the app, then fetch. But dev server needs the dev cert and is the source dev path. Let me try npm start and curl the dev URL. Actually the guide's method is the build. The summary says dev server verified on port 5175.

Let me try a different operational check: run the project's test suite? That's heavy and not required. 

Let me attempt running the built app with a real headless browser. None installed. Can't install (prohibited).

Let me try jsdom with the module transformed... too complex.

Given constraints, the strongest evidence available: build artifacts complete, all referenced assets serve with correct content types, bundle syntax valid, HTML entry correct. Let me also verify the bundle actually contains the app mount code and config loading logic, and check the locales resources referenced by config.

Let me check that config references resolve: portalLocales, etc. And check the resources referenced from config: services.json, rest-services.json, style_v3.json all exist in basic/resources — verified.

Let me try to run the dev server (vite) which is the documented dev path, and fetch the transformed index. That gives evidence the app compiles and serves. But starting vite may write files (cert). Allowed - normal runtime file creation. Let me try.

Actually let me first attempt a jsdom-based execution of the bundle using vite's SSR or by transforming. Hmm.

Let me try simply: npm start in background, wait, curl https://localhost:5173 with -k.

But that uses the dev source, not the built dist. The task is to validate the installation which produced dist build. Both matter. Let me try dev server to confirm the software runs.

Actually, let me reconsider. Vite dev server serves the source app. That confirms operational. Let me try.
